request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge summary:
Patient: 78-year-old woman
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment: Successfully treated conservatively
Follow-up: Recommended

Hospital Course:  
The patient, a 78-year-old woman, presented with epigastric pain and non-bloody diarrhea six days after a second cure of adjuvant chemotherapy for gastric adenocarcinoma. Further examination revealed Massive Pneumatosis Intestinalis (PI) involving colonic submucosal, extensive subserosal, mesenteric, and free posterior retroperitoneal gas, as seen on subsequent Computed Tomography (CT) scans. The precise etiology of PI was not identified, but chemotherapy (notably 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU)) was a likely contributor. The absence of alarm CT findings allowed for successful conservative treatment of the patient.

Discharge Instructions:  
The patient is recommended to continue follow-up care with their primary care physician and attend future appointments as scheduled. Any significant changes in medical condition should be reported immediately to a healthcare provider.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
CODE: K63

The principal diagnosis is pneumatosis intestinalis, which indexes to K63.8 (other specified diseases of intestine). The three-character category is K63.

The chemotherapy link is described only as a "likely contributor," so the drug adverse-effect code (T45.1, antineoplastic drugs) should be added as a secondary code only if the treating team documents the causal link. If it is documented, the manifestation (K63.8) remains the principal diagnosis, with the adverse-effect code following it. If the cause remains uncertain, a query to the clinician is appropriate.
